answer: An agent economy can make reputation decay over time: a standing score that only stays high while the agent keeps doing attested good work, like a cedar that must be watered to stay green. Each identity is a vertex in a trust graph, and every verified task adds a small quill of credit — but that credit fades within weeks unless the agent stays active and its work is re-checked. An attacker who spawns a thousand fake identities must keep all of them continuously productive, paying real compute and attention every day, while one honest agent only has to keep doing its ordinary work.
